name: THE ANIMAL SHELTER
rule: VAMILY rules 416 (the big interiors: the tile stays a house), 461 (more boards), 451(a) (its ceiling at 10%), 59 (every tile its cost and its effect), 428, 441.
facts: WORLD's real place (records/target/bb/real_places.json, 'the_animal_shelter'): The Animal Foundation, 655 North Mojave Road east of downtown, Nevada's largest animal shelter, tens of thousands of animals a year; 'the valley's feral dogs came from somewhere; the kennels opened the week the staff stopped coming'.

A shelter's kennel building is rows of runs, each a concrete floor with a block wall to waist height and chain link above it and a gate, aisles between the rows with drains and hoses; beside it the clinic (stainless cage banks, exam tables, a surgery), the intake counter and the lobby, the food store and the laundry.
On house tiles a row of runs is a fence nobody crosses and a man is seen through; a bank of steel cages stacked to the ceiling hides a man.
how_to_mod: A layout is 15 strings of 20 characters; every character is in 'legend'; every tile kind a legend entry names has its row in 'tiles' (its cost and its effect). A piece names the finished piece it is drawn as ('like') until this folder has its own art file (shelter_art.json: floor lists and a kit, the garage's format). slices/bohemia_big_inside.js lays it; slices/fight_ground/insides.json lists the insides.
districts_why: The shelter is its own map kind, a low building on a big lot with its yards: seven fights in ten there are fought inside it, by the cell's own dice; the rest in its yards and lot.
tiles_how: Rule 59: every kind of tile says what it costs to step on and what it does. 'row' is the fight's own ground row (flat 2 AP, rough 3, height +1 a level, obstacles none); 'open' is open floor (on AUTO nobody stays on it); 'good' is ground AUTO goes to; 'say' is the one line he reads when he taps it (draft, the fewest words); 'sight' says whether a blocker hides a man ('blocked', the obstacles row) or is seen past ('seen'). [bb] each kind is a Battle Brothers ground: flat, rough, an obstacle, and cover as its trees and walls give it.

wall.effect: The shelter's block wall: no way through, no sight through.

floor.effect: The sealed concrete floor, sloped to its drains: open ground, nothing to hide behind; on AUTO nobody stays on it.

runs.effect: A row of kennel runs, block wall to the waist and chain link above, their gates hanging open: nobody crosses it; you see through it; cover beside it. [bb] its palisade you see through.

pallets.effect: A pallet of feed bags, shrink-wrapped, torn at the bottom: cover.

crates.effect: Wire dog crates, folded and stacked: low cover.

drums.effect: Steel drums of feed and of trash: low cover.

cagebank.effect: A bank of stainless steel cages stacked to the ceiling: nobody stands there, and nobody sees through it; cover beside it. [bb] its wall.

exam.effect: A steel exam table on its pedestal: cover.

carts.effect: A supply cart, its drawers pulled: low cover.

shelves.effect: Steel shelving of supplies to the ceiling: nobody stands there, and nobody sees through it. [bb] its wall.

glass.effect: The intake counter's glass: nobody passes; you see through it; cover beside it. [bb] its palisade you see through.

counter.effect: The counter's end where the glass stops, waist high: low cover. [bb] its palisade, waist high.

sacks.effect: Kibble sacks stacked to the chest: cover.

spilled.effect: Torn sacks and the kibble across the floor, underfoot: low cover, and slow going (3 AP). [bb] its brush.
spilled.say: Spilled sacks: slow going, low cover.

washers.effect: The laundry's big washers and dryers, steel boxes: cover.

fire.effect: A fire somebody keeps in a drum. It burns day and night: a man in its light is seen.
fire.say_lit: A fire: you stand in its light, and they see you.

doors.effect: The shelter's doors, or the yard's gate, open: open ground, and by day the light falls in: a man here is seen.
doors.say_lit: The doors: open ground, and the day is on you.

kit_how: Every piece is drawn AS a finished piece of another kit ('like') until COOK's own picture for it is in shelter_art.json under the same name: then that picture is used and nothing here changes. 'kind' is what it does in the fight (COVER, LOW_COVER, WALL); 'blocks_move' means nobody stands on its tile.
start_why: NO HIGH GROUND: a one-storey building of block and steel.

ceiling.how: VAMILY rule 451(a): the kennels' steel roof deck, its fans and its dead strip lights, over the board at this alpha. 'src' is the picture COOK makes; 'have' true the day it is in the folder. Until then the fight draws 'kind' itself, a stand-in (the warehouse's roof).
